topic:
Flat-strip completion of the thickness-multiplicity frontier for boundary causal traces. This is a new attempt at banked parent stat_bdd_thickness_estimability_frontier, not a retry of its circular annulus witness. Observe iid O=(X,T,Y), X=(R,S) in [-1,1]^2, T=1{R>=0}, on B={(0,s):|s|<=1/2}; target the contrast of unique bounded L-Lipschitz observed-side traces under conditionally sigma-sub-Gaussian errors. For q_t(x,h)=P{X in side t and B_2(x,h)}, impose common lower mass c_m h^kappa. Let J_P(h,u) be the h-packing number of boundary sites with min_t q_t(x,h)<=u. Define isolated laws by one threshold-thin site plus J_P(h,u)<=C_iso{1+h^-1(u/h^2)^(1/(kappa-2))}, and pervasive laws by J_P(h,C_m h^kappa)>=c_J/h. Prove explicit normalized Cartesian product/radial-power laws and Gaussian tent alternatives make both classes nonempty. Prove matched expected-sup risks n^-1/(kappa+2) and (log n/n)^1/(kappa+2), one kappa-free count estimator attaining the pervasive/base rate, and an explicit finite-pattern band with finite-sample simultaneous coverage over every declared nonempty triangular profile union and matching pervasive all-band expected-width lower bound. Do not use circular coordinates, unit-circle packing, the parent's vacuous side-mass placeholder, or claim arbitrary-profile/local-oracle band exactness. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Writing alpha=kappa-2, the flat pervasive density normalizes as (kappa-1)|r|^alpha/4, while the clipped radial-power law has explicit normalizer 4-V_alpha/(alpha+2). Cartesian rectangles and half-balls give uniform one-sided h^kappa masses, including both segment endpoints, and imply the full isolated J_P envelope. Severity-layer peeling yields the isolated no-log upper bound; deterministic boundary grids, finite-pattern calibration, and Gaussian tents give the pervasive lower and band routes. At kappa=3 the pervasive tent product KL is nL^2h^5/(480 sigma^2). Checks covered 78 mass configurations, large-radius clipping, u=1, asymmetric sides, empty counts, and endpoint geometry; constants are uniform only on compact exponent sets bounded away from 2, and the observed-side regressions themselves remain L-Lipschitz. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently formalize the combined normalized flat witness membership and tent-validity theorem, including Borel laws, support, conditional kernels, all mass/profile inequalities, target separations, and Gaussian product KL with the declared target segment. EARLY KILL TEST: Verify the draft's equations (2.1)-(2.6) and construct the actual observed Gaussian laws for both endpoints, clipped radii, u=1, and the smallest admitted exponent; stop if any membership inequality must be assumed. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_bdd_flatstrip_thickness_entropy_frontier.md.

D-1 SCOPE AUDIT (controlling accepted scope): The exploratory topic above proposed matched lower bounds and a finite-pattern simultaneous-confidence-band/width program. Across D-1 revision, the accepted kernel was explicitly narrowed to the total global-bandwidth profile-adaptive estimator and its isolated, pervasive, and regular expected-sup risk conclusions. The confidence-band/width program was withdrawn and is not delivered here; no finite selector, packing event, or anchor construction is a confidence band. Exact endpoint lower bounds, if restated, are attributed supporting converses from the banked parent rather than a new novelty claim. The note’s novelty is simultaneous cross-regime attainment by the present estimator.

source_refs.claim: Derives pointwise minimax rates under polynomially vanishing random-design density, but not a normalized many-site boundary construction or packing-profile theorem.
source_refs.author: Stéphane Gaïffas

source_refs.claim: Studies a treatment-effect curve along a bivariate assignment boundary under a score density bounded away from zero, leaving polynomially vanishing one-sided boundary mass outside its regime.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocío Titiunik, and Ruiqi Rae Yu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked parent closed its statistical reductions but never constructed the load-bearing probability laws: the normalized measure, Borel conditional kernels, side-mass bounds, packing profiles, tent preservation, target separation, and KL calculations remained axiomatized. The literature supplies single-site degenerate-design calculations and regular-density boundary-curve inference, but not their combination. In the flat replacement, the first proof step must derive every mass and profile inequality from Cartesian or clipped radial-power densities using exact rectangle and half-ball geometry, including segment endpoints, clipped radii, asymmetric sides, u=1, and the smallest admitted exponent. The Gaussian alternatives must then preserve bounded Lipschitz observed-side regressions and yield the claimed n-fold KL without assuming membership.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A single explicit theorem constructing normalized Borel flat-strip laws and Gaussian tent experiments, proving all base, isolated, and pervasive mass/profile inequalities, trace separations, and an exact constant-level n-fold product-KL bound uniformly on compact exponent sets bounded away from 2.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation treats the whole assignment-boundary effect curve as the causal object and links boundary geometry to uniform inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: multi-score assignment creates a boundary effect curve -> uniform recovery depends on one-sided local information -> polynomial thinning may occur at one or many sites -> explicit flat laws must certify the thickness-multiplicity frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the polynomial local-mass bias-information calculation and localized Gaussian alternative proof, replacing one degenerate point by side-valid flat-boundary tents.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its single-site information scale is the direct donor for the h-to-the-kappa tent KL calculation required by the flat witness.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the separated Gaussian bump-packing lower-bound argument, replacing a positive density minimum by explicit one-sided polynomial masses and boundary packing counts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the structurally analogous transition from one local regression difficulty to a logarithmic sup-norm obstruction over many sites.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the boundary-indexed local-regression formulation while replacing its uniformly positive-density Gram and variance controls with explicit flat-law count bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The estimand is already a causal contrast indexed by a bivariate treatment boundary; the missing ingredient is the nonregular design geometry.

open_problems.open_problem: For a positive nondecreasing two-sided tube-mass modulus and declared lower and upper thin-site packing profiles, what exact oracle functional characterizes expected-sup minimax trace risk and uniform consistency across polynomial and severe exponential regimes?

source_refs.excerpt: characterize R_n(P(m,J_-)) by matching same-class upper and lower bounds
For an arbitrary slack lower packing declaration, the lower display need not match the upper display
Promote the arbitrary-modulus handle into one named profile theorem for a non-polynomial class

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent proves only a bracket: its upper bound pays global boundary entropy, whereas its lower bound depends on the declared lower thin-site profile, so slack declarations can leave polynomially different quantities. Closing the bracket requires identifying the upper-profile regularity that permits severity-layer estimation and the lower-profile realizability conditions that support simultaneous legal packed alternatives. Severe moduli also change the information equation and can yield logarithmically slow consistency, so the polynomial calculation cannot simply be extrapolated.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A same-class two-sided minimax theorem equating risk up to constants to an explicit bias-information-entropy oracle functional, with an adaptive bandwidth rule, an if-and-only-if triangular-union consistency criterion, and worked polynomial and exponential-modulus corollaries.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from boundary identification to geometry-dependent uniform risk is the natural narrative to generalize beyond regular or polynomial thickness.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: a boundary trace is identified from one-sided observations -> regular thickness yields a familiar uniform rate -> arbitrary thinning changes local information and effective multiplicity -> characterize the complete modulus-profile risk frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize the bias-versus-local-mass information equation and localized minimax alternatives from regularly varying one-point designs to arbitrary moduli and boundary packings.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its pointwise rate equation supplies the local-information component of the desired boundary-uniform oracle.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over spatially inhomogeneous normalization and multiscale uniform control, replacing density-indexed rates by two-sided tube-mass and packing-profile functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It addresses uniform regression loss under spatially varying information, the same structure enriched here by causal sides and explicit thin-site entropy.

open_problems.open_problem: What profile-separation condition is necessary and sufficient for one data-measurable confidence band to attain local-oracle expected widths over triangular unions of isolated and pervasive boundary-thickness laws while retaining simultaneous coverage?

source_refs.claim: Constructs asymptotically honest adaptive confidence bands through Gaussian approximation and anti-concentration, but does not cover finite-sample polynomially sparse boundary cells.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

source_refs.claim: Shows that honest smoothness-adaptive bands require restrictions such as self-similarity, providing a testing-based template but not a thin-site profile criterion.
source_refs.author: Adam D. Bull

source_refs.claim: Derives finite-sample honest confidence intervals and modulus lower bounds for scalar regression functionals, not locally adaptive bands for a boundary curve.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong and Michal Kolesár

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent's finite-pattern band is globally honest and rate-matched on pervasive classes, but its calibration pays a global log n factor even where local multiplicity is bounded, while its local-width converse relies on a growing pervasive codebook and therefore leaves isolated-only unions unresolved. Generic adaptive-band theory addresses smoothness adaptation under regular designs, and scalar modulus theory does not encode many locally sparse sites. Moreover, score-law total variation alone cannot characterize adaptation because equal score laws may have distinguishable outcome kernels. The missing proof step is a locally indexed conditional calibration or a matching full-observed-law testing criterion that separates exactly those profile unions permitting local-width adaptation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving an explicit, checkable profile-separation condition under which a finite-pattern or multiplier band has simultaneous coverage and expected half-width uniformly comparable to the local oracle benchmark, together with a full-law testing converse proving failure when that condition is violated.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly motivates simultaneous uncertainty for an entire boundary treatment-effect curve and supplies the regular-density benchmark.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: substantive conclusions concern a whole boundary curve -> simultaneous bands are required -> local information may vary from one thin site to a pervasive set -> determine when honest width can adapt to that profile

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt Gaussian anti-concentration, multiplier calibration, and data-selected resolution control to a location-and-scale index with random sparse cells.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof architecture controls a data-dependent supremum; the new criterion must prevent that calibration from retaining a global entropy penalty at isolated sites.

method_exemplars.technique: Use worst-case Lipschitz bias and modulus-of-continuity arguments to relate honest expected width to distinguishability over convex regression classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a finite-sample causal-inference template for both attainable honest width and a matching adaptation converse.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the confidence-band-to-testing reduction and separated multi-alternative construction from smoothness classes to thickness-profile unions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired necessity result is structurally an honest-adaptation impossibility theorem, with design multiplicity replacing unknown smoothness.

open_problems.open_problem: Which primitive flat-strip density and support conditions make scalar one-sided h-to-the-kappa mass sufficient for uniform signed-distance local-polynomial Gram coercivity, and when can the same mass coexist with asymptotically singular Gram matrices?

source_refs.excerpt: For local-polynomial degree above zero, scalar mass still does not imply Gram coercivity
which local-mass and density hypotheses imply the uniform Gram lower bound needed for the local-polynomial upper
a verifiable sufficient-condition corollary for polygonal and smooth GIS partitions

open_problems.why_unsolved: Scalar neighborhood mass controls the number of observations but permits concentration at signed-distance radii that make higher-order moment columns nearly collinear. The local-constant count proof therefore cannot be reused: its scalar denominator must be replaced by quantitative minimum-eigenvalue bounds for two side-specific random Gram matrices. A resolution needs radial-balance or subannulus conditions derived from primitive flat support and density geometry, plus counterexamples showing exactly what scalar mass alone fails to control.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp sufficient-condition theorem, paired with a singular-design counterexample or necessary-and-sufficient characterization, translating flat-strip density, cone or cusp geometry, and radial-balance constants into explicit h-dependent lower eigenvalue bounds for every declared polynomial degree.

writing_exemplar.why: Its signed-distance local-polynomial formulation exposes the gap between interpretable assignment geometry and abstract Gram regularity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: boundary local polynomials require invertible distance moments -> abstract Gram assumptions are hard to verify -> scalar neighborhood mass does not prevent radial degeneracy -> derive primitive geometric coercivity conditions

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze local-polynomial normal equations in intrinsic coordinates and derive matrix conditioning from local support geometry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result likewise converts explicit neighborhood geometry into quantitative local moment-matrix behavior.

method_exemplars.technique: Express boundary estimators through side-specific signed-distance Gram matrices and propagate eigenvalue control into uniform stochastic bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those are exactly the estimator and proof steps that primitive flat-strip conditions must validate.

literature_map:
Gaïffas (2005, Mathematical Methods of Statistics, arXiv:math/0410354) derives pointwise minimax rates at a single vanishing-density design point.
Gaïffas (2007, ESAIM: Probability and Statistics, DOI 10.1051/ps:2007023) adapts to unknown local design and smoothness at one point, with an unavoidable logarithmic price for that joint adaptation problem.
Gaïffas (2005, arXiv:math/0509634) gives spatially varying sharp sup-norm rates indexed by design density, but not a packing-profile frontier at density zeros.
Hengartner and Linton (1996, Canadian Journal of Statistics, DOI 10.2307/3315335) establish pointwise asymptotics at isolated design poles and zeros.
Bertin (2004, Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference, DOI 10.1016/S0378-3758(03)00154-X) obtains an exact random-design sup-norm constant while assuming density bounded away from zero.
Antoniadis, Pensky, and Sapatinas (2014, ESAIM: Probability and Statistics, DOI 10.1051/ps/2012024) study finitely many density zeros under global L2 loss and known inhomogeneous design.
Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001, Econometrica, DOI 10.1111/1468-0262.00183) anchor causal identification of the scalar regression-discontinuity contrast.
Imbens and Wager (2019, Review of Economics and Statistics, arXiv:1705.01677) give conditional finite-sample-minimax scalar RD inference and allow multiple running variables.
Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2025, arXiv:2505.05670) study pointwise and uniform estimation of a boundary treatment-effect curve but assume score density bounded away from zero.
Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2026, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2510.26051) tie boundary geometry to uniform inference and isotropic minimax rates, again under regular positive density.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2018, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA14434) provide finite-sample optimal honest intervals for scalar regression functionals over convex smoothness classes.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2020, Quantitative Economics, DOI 10.3982/QE1199) turn worst-case smoothing bias into simple honest scalar nonparametric and RD intervals.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/14-AOS1235) provide anti-concentration and multiplier-bootstrap machinery for asymptotically honest adaptive bands.
Bull (2012, Electronic Journal of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/12-EJS720) proves that honest smoothness-adaptive bands require restrictions such as self-similarity.
The unoccupied intersection is polynomial one-sided boundary mass, the multiplicity of thin sites, causal trace geometry, and finite-sample simultaneous honesty.
